heading: What `linear_scan: false` does not restrict
text:
## What `linear_scan: false` does not restrict [LNLS.10]

The following are fully available in `linear_scan: false` programs:

- All numeric types (Int, Float, Bool) and all their operations.
- String slots, interned string literals, string comparisons using
  `==` and `!=` (always O(1); no annotation needed).
- `len(s)` — O(1) for interned strings; no annotation needed.
- Single-pattern `where` clauses with any numeric comparison operator.
- String ordering `<`/`>`/`<=`/`>=` in single-pattern position
  on slots with `capacity` (LNLS.3.10).
- Regex match on slots with a declared `capacity` (LNLS.3.7).
- All fact lifecycle types (`logical`, `ttl`).
- All schema slot markers (`retained`, `tolerance` with
  at least one non-tolerance anchor slot).
- Cooldown rules (the `cooldown` modifier).
- TMS / logical facts (the `logical` lifecycle and `emit X logical`).
- `then` / temporal sequencing, within the equality-anchor
  constraint of [LNLS.4.11].
- `call`, `cache`, `publish`, `log`, `emit` actions.
- Any series aggregation not listed in LNLS.3.5.
- All arithmetic operators.
- `now()` and `dwell` time expressions.
- Imports and multi-file programs.
- `const` declarations (string literals only — already compile-time constants).
- The `.dstest` test surface.
